title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie

lessons.title: Don't Criticize, Condemn or Complain
lessons.key_idea: Criticism makes people defensive and resentful, so it almost never changes behaviour. Understanding them works far better.
issues: scene 6: Below the 'Why?' box and the three check circles there are two disconnected curved strokes. They read as a broken drawing, perhaps an unfinished face or open hands, and do not clearly illustrate 'reasons that make sense to them'. (fix: Replace the two loose arcs with a clear element, such as a simple person figure holding the checkmarks or a thought bubble containing them. Otherwise remove the arcs so the 'Why?' box, checks and label stand on their own.)

lessons.title: Everyone Craves Feeling Important
lessons.key_idea: The deepest human hunger is to feel appreciated, so honest and sincere appreciation is one of the most powerful tools you have.

lessons.title: Talk About What They Want
lessons.key_idea: To move someone to act, stop talking about what you want and show them how it gets them what they want.
issues: scene 3: The calf, housemaid and barn are crammed into the right third of the stage, leaving the left two-thirds empty above the ground line. Emerson and his son, the pushing and pulling the narration describes, are not drawn at all. The housemaid also overlaps the barn doorway outline. (fix: Add two figures for Emerson and his son: one pushing behind the calf, one pulling in front, with the calf's legs braced. Spread the group across the full ground line so the scene is centred. Place the housemaid clearly in front of the barn so she no longer overlaps the door outline.)

lessons.title: Be Interested, Not Interesting
lessons.key_idea: You make more friends by being genuinely curious about others, listening well and remembering their names than by trying to impress them.

lessons.title: Nobody Wins an Argument
lessons.key_idea: Even when you win an argument, you lose the person, so the best way to come out ahead is to avoid the fight altogether.

lessons.title: Admit Mistakes, Let Others Save Face
lessons.key_idea: Admitting your own errors quickly and letting others keep their dignity disarms resistance and makes change easier to accept.

lessons.title: See the World Through Their Eyes
lessons.key_idea: Every principle in the book comes from one sincere habit: honestly trying to see things from the other person's point of view.

plan.title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
plan.author: Dale Carnegie
plan.confidence_note: I know this widely read 1936 classic well, including its four-part structure and its core principles for handling people.
plan.one_liner: Stop trying to win arguments and start making people feel important. That changes everything.
plan.summary: First published in 1936, Dale Carnegie's classic grew out of the courses he taught adults on speaking and dealing with people. His core belief is simple: people are driven by emotion and pride far more than logic, and almost everyone deeply wants to feel important. The book is organised into practical principles. It shows how to handle people without stirring up resentment, how to make others genuinely like you, how to win people to your way of thinking without arguing, and how to change behaviour without giving offence. Carnegie illustrates each idea with stories of business leaders, historical figures and his own students. Above all, he insists these methods only work when they are sincere. Flattery and manipulation backfire. Real curiosity, appreciation and respect for the other person's point of view are what open doors.
